images.alt: A dome of thin saplings stuck in the ground and bent over into crossing hoops, before thatching
images.caption: The frame of a beehive hut: switches stuck into the ground round the floor and bent over into crossing hoops. Roth's 'Northern Coast-line', the Bloomfield to Princess Charlotte Bay type.
images.credit: Photograph: W. E. Roth, North Queensland Ethnography Bulletin 16 (Records of the Australian Museum 8, 1910), Plate XVI fig. 1

images.alt: Low bark-roofed platform huts on forked posts among river trees
images.caption: Composite huts at the junction of the Palmer and Mitchell Rivers in 1899: sleeping platforms on forked posts, roofed with bark. The nearest old photograph of a house on the Mitchell. Cropped to the huts.
images.credit: Photograph: Sub-Inspector Garraway, 1899, in W. E. Roth, North Queensland Ethnography Bulletin 16 (1910), Plate XIII fig. 2
images.location: Junction of the Palmer and Mitchell Rivers, 1899

images.alt: A low rounded hut thickly thatched with grass, with a small dark entrance
images.caption: A finished grass-thatched hut with its small entrance, at Normanton on the Gulf: the same dome under a different thatch.
images.credit: Photograph: W. E. Roth, North Queensland Ethnography Bulletin 16 (Records of the Australian Museum 8, 1910), Plate XIV fig. 1

images.alt: A dome hut covered in leafy bushes with an arched doorway
images.caption: A sapling-framed hut covered with bushes, in the north-west districts; the leaves go on from the top down.
images.credit: Photograph: W. E. Roth, North Queensland Ethnography Bulletin 16 (Records of the Australian Museum 8, 1910), Plate XVII fig. 1

images.alt: A single sheet of bark propped on edge in sand with a stick
images.caption: The simplest shelter: one sheet of bark fixed lengthways and edgeways in the ground.
images.credit: Photograph: W. E. Roth, North Queensland Ethnography Bulletin 16 (Records of the Australian Museum 8, 1910), Plate XIII fig. 1

images.alt: A sheet of bark bent over into a low tent shape on sand
images.caption: A single bark sheet bent at the middle with its ends fixed in the soil: the bark tent of the dry country.
images.credit: Photograph: W. E. Roth, North Queensland Ethnography Bulletin 16 (Records of the Australian Museum 8, 1910), Plate XVI fig. 2
